questions.prompt: Which instruction best follows the advice to say what to do rather than what not to do?

options.text: No bullets, no headings, no bold.
Write your answer as smoothly flowing prose paragraphs.

questions.explanation: Describing the destination (flowing prose) works better than listing things to avoid, which still leaves the model guessing what you do want.

questions.prompt: Your code will parse the model's output. Which steps help? Select all that apply.

options.text: Specify the exact format and show an example
Tell the model to reply with only the record, no introduction
Define what to output when information is missing
Skip validation because the model usually gets it right

questions.explanation: Exact format, no extras, and a defined empty case make output parseable. You should still validate in code and plan a retry.

questions.prompt: Giving the model a skeleton with placeholders to fill exactly is called the ____ pattern.
questions.explanation: The Template pattern trades some creativity for consistency and predictability.

questions.prompt: You set a low output token limit to get short answers. What actually happens?

options.text: The model plans a shorter, complete answer
The response is cut off when the limit is reached, possibly mid-sentence
The limit is converted into a word count

questions.explanation: A token limit truncates. Ask for brevity in the prompt (in words or sentences) and use the limit only as a safety cap.

questions.prompt: Match each vague constraint to a concrete replacement.

pairs.right: Words a 12-year-old knows; define technical terms
Formal, no slang, no exclamation marks
Use only facts in <notes>; write 'not provided' if missing

questions.explanation: Concrete constraints are checkable, so both you and the model know whether they were met.

questions.prompt: Order the steps for producing machine-readable output.

items.text: Specify the exact format with an example
Retry or flag outputs that fail validation
Define the empty or missing-data case

questions.explanation: Define the format and the empty case in the prompt, then validate in code and handle failures.
